description: Widen the single-CTA panel block width nb beyond 32 on n=512/1024 to cut the panel-loop iteration count (n/nb panels, each = a panel kernel launch + a trailing GEMM). The panel kernel's SMEM buffers (red[MAXCB*16], wsh[MAXCB], the cb-wide T-factor) HARD-CAP cb at 32 — raise MAXCB to 48/64, restructure those SMEM buffers (or move T to a padded SMEM tile), and sweep nb in {32,48,64}. Fewer/wider panels = fewer trailing-GEMM launches and fewer panel-kernel launches (the panel is ~50-60% of n=512 time and launch/latency-sensitive). The 2-level IB micro-panel already makes wide cb viable WITHOUT the quadratic serial-trailing blowup (a sibling measured cb=32 2-level is 2.3x faster than cb=32 single-level), so wider nb should now pay. FP32 panel. Keep n!=512/1024 as parent (b050aa33). Avoid the substring 'stream' incl. comments.

Widen panel nb: MAXCB 32->64, n=512 cb=64, n=1024 cb=48. Generalized kernel ldv!=cb so nb need not divide n; T-factor tile overlays dead block-apply scratch; T recurrence driven by tid so cb>32. All 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN. REGRESSION: geomean 10967us (min-of-2 10967/10984, <0.2% spread = stable, not contention) = 2.5x SLOWER than parent 4358us. nsys n=512: panel 94.5%, 8 panels x 3.39M ns = 27.1M ns vs cb=32's 16 x 337k = 5.4M ns (5x slower per-launch). cb=64 SMEM ~178KB/CTA forces 1 CTA/SM (cb=32 ~70KB = 3 CTAs/SM); occupancy collapse + fused-w_c work scaling with cb beat the halved launch count.

nb=48 for n=512 AND n=1024 (non-divisor -> ragged panels: n=512 11 panels 10x48+32, n=1024 22 panels 21x48+16). Partial-panel ldv!=cb path validates CLEAN. geomean min-of-2 14623us (14623/14646, stable) = WORSE than parent 4358us and worse than cb=64 (10967us). cb=48 is the worst sweep point: >32-wide panels lose occupancy AND non-divisor raggedness gives MORE panels than cb=64 (11 vs 8). Confirms P=(m+1)*cb SMEM scales with cb -> occupancy collapse beats launch-count reduction.

Widen ONLY n=1024 panel nb 32->48 (n=512 kept at parent cb=32 since cb>32 collapses occupancy; IB=8). All 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN. min-of-3 geomean 9475.7us (9505/9499/9476) under ~2.4x contention (n=512 dense ~20.7k vs ~8.7k clean). SAME-CONTENTION A/B: n1024=48 -> 9475.7 vs n1024=32(parent-eq) -> 9441.6 = lever is ~0.4% WORSE. WHY: nsys total-GPU-kernel-time n=1024 dense cb=32=18.33M ns vs cb=48=18.61M ns -- the 28% panel-kernel saving (20.36M->14.63M, 32->22 panels) is offset by ~6M ns LARGER trailing GEMMs; total O(n^3) work conserved (rank-cb update shifts panel->GEMM), shape is ~90% GPU-bound so flat GPU time=flat benchmark. n=512 cb=64 SMEM 178KB->1 CTA/SM=2.5x regression; cb=48 ragged=worse; IB=16 at cb=48=28.4M ns (spill). nb=32 optimal for both n=512 and n=1024.

Swept the wide-panel lever (nb in {32,48,64}) for n=512 and n=1024; built the generalization that unblocks ANY nb (kernel now takes ldv=workspace-leading-dim separately from cb=active-width, so nb need NOT divide n -- the T-factor tile overlays the dead block-apply scratch, T recurrence driven by tid so cb can exceed 32). All configs validate CLEAN (22 tests + 3 guards). HEAD=0d71602 (n=512 cb=32, n=1024 cb=48, IB=8), min-of-3 geomean 9475.7us under ~2.4x contention.

MEASURED VERDICT -- the lever does NOT pay at the benchmark level, for a profile-confirmed reason: total O(n^3) GPU work is CONSERVED when nb widens (the rank-cb update the panel KERNEL sheds just moves into a WIDER trailing T^T V^T C GEMM). nsys total-GPU-kernel-time, n=1024 dense (contention-immune): cb=32=18.33M ns vs cb=48=18.61M ns -- the panel kernel got 28% faster (20.36M->14.63M, 32->22 panels) but the trailing GEMMs grew ~6M ns. Same-contention A/B: n1024=48 9475.7us vs n1024=32 9441.6us = lever ~0.4% WORSE. At n=512 it is far worse: cb=64 SMEM 178KB/CTA forces 1 CTA/SM (cb=32 was ~70KB=3 CTAs/SM) -> panel 5x slower per-launch -> 2.5x geomean regression (10967us); cb=48 ragged-panel = worst (14623us). IB re-tune at cb=48 (IB=16) made it worse (28.4M ns, register spill) and CANNOT help since the GEMM growth -- not the panel -- is the gap. nb=32 stays optimal for BOTH shapes.

STILL OPEN (directions this measurement uncovered, for the manager to weigh): (1) The trailing GEMM, not the panel, is now the lever at n=1024/2048 -- it grew to ~15-23% (cb=48) and the wider 128x256 TF32 GEMM tiles are where the conserved work lives; attacking GEMM efficiency / fusing the 3 bmm calls (V^T C, T^T W, C-=VW) could beat what panel-width cannot. (2) The ldv!=cb generalization I added makes the panel workspace decoupled from the active width -- it enables a LEFT-LOOKING/look-ahead panel (factor a narrow leading sub-block while a wide trailing GEMM runs) without the divisor constraint, a different lever than raw width. (3) n=1024 B=60 is GPU-bound (~90%) but SM-under-occupied at cb=32 (1 CTA/SM, P=131KB); a panel that caches FEWER rows in SMEM (not the full m=1024) would raise occupancy AND allow wider cb -- the real unlock the raw-width lever cannot reach because P=(m+1)*cb is the occupancy wall. I did not build (1)/(2)/(3); they are off this brief's narrow 'widen nb' objective.
